resources.string: Square Chess began as a project to make chess feel at home on compact, nearly square Android displays, starting with the Unihertz Titan 2 Elite. It is designed to work across compatible Android devices. Play against the computer, play locally with another person, or record a game played on a real board. Built independently by DataEspresso.

Tap a piece, then its destination. Legal destinations are marked. Use Review to step through earlier moves, then Return to resume your game. Undo asks for confirmation. Menu contains additional actions, including Flip board and Save & home. Games save after each confirmed move.

Games and settings stay on this device. This build has no accounts, advertising, analytics or automatic telemetry. Gameplay and these help pages work without a connection.

Feedback is shared only when you choose to send it with your email app. You can preview and edit the entire message first. Optional bug-report details include only the app version, device manufacturer/model, Android version and game mode. Reports do not automatically include identifiers, saved games, moves, positions, screenshots or logs. Your email app may add your email address or signature.

Feedback drafts are kept temporarily so you can return to them; Square Chess does not upload them or send email itself.
A public privacy-policy page has not been published yet. No external policy link is configured for this development build.

This experimental build includes Fairy-Stockfish and the pinned Lichess native wrapper under GPLv3. Classical evaluation is used; no NNUE network is bundled. Chesslib and the Chessnut artwork use Apache 2.0. The licences and notices below are available without a connection. Source and build-material obligations still apply when distributing covered binaries; the development repository is private and is not a public source-download link.
